item.title: Excluding Windows Reserved Ports
item.description: When starting a service, you may occasionally encounter a situation where a port is occupied. However, when you actually query it using netstat -ano | findstr :[prot], you might find that no program is occupying it. This is usually because it has been occupied by Windows as a reserved port. item.title: Remove Windows Network Addresses (FTP) from Quick Access
item.description: No direct fix, but you can clear all custom Quick Access entries (resets to default). Go to C:\\Users\\YourUsername\\AppData\\Roaming\\Microsoft\\Windows\\Recent\\AutomaticDestinations. Back up all files in that folder, then nuke ’em. References FTP address cannot be removed from Quick Access, other folders can – Microsoft Community
